, Reason for Mistake: The agent hallucinated the source data. It claimed that according to "Girls Who Code," the percentage of women in computer science was 37% in 1995 and dropped to 24% in 2025. In reality, Girls Who Code is an organization founded in 2012 to close the gender gap; they do not possess historical data from 1995 stating that 37% of CS professionals were women. The actual statistic (women comprising ~37% of CS degrees around 1995) comes from US Census data or NSF reports, not Girls Who Code. By fabricating the source attribution, the agent provided factually incorrect reasoning for the final answer.
